rules.statement: Consumer sets i_rd_en = 1 at the first read edge after seeing o_empty = 0, keeps it, and drops it at the edge of the 24th accepted read.
All inputs i_wr_en, i_wr_data and i_rd_en change only at rising edges of their own clock.

rules.condition: back-to-back write burst with equal clocks and i_wr_en = 1
rules.statement: A word is accepted at every write edge during the burst and o_full stays 0 for the whole burst.

rules.condition: back-to-back read burst from first to last accepted read
rules.statement: A word is accepted at every read edge, o_empty stays 0 until the last word is read, and o_rd_data steps through consecutive words in write order.

rules.condition: after start-up delay with equal clocks, until writes stop
rules.statement: The number of words in the FIFO stays at 4 (write pointer minus read pointer counted at read edges) in steady state.
Both Gray pointers change by one bit at every edge, and pointer wrap from 15 to 0 with storage address wrap from 7 to 0 has no effect on flow.
No o_overflow or o_underflow pulse occurs during the burst.
With a slower read clock the FIFO fills and o_full stops the producer; with a faster read clock o_empty stops the consumer.
The tool bin and lib directories of the suite shall both be on PATH.
The software reset returns the FIFO to the empty state without a hardware reset.

rules.condition: from the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0
rules.statement: Writes are blocked from the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0, combinationally with zero latency.
The write reset FSM raises req_wr at the next write edge, and it crosses to the read domain.
When the synchronized request is 1, reads are blocked (rd_blk) and o_empty = 1.
The read reset FSM resets the read pointer to 0 and then raises ack_rd, which crosses to the write domain.

rules.condition: acknowledge not yet seen by write side
rules.statement: The write pointer is reset only after the acknowledge is seen, never before the read side has stopped using the old pointer.
The write FSM holds, with writes blocked, until i_rst_n_sw = 1.
The write side drops the request, the read side drops the acknowledge, and each side leaves reset only when its synchronized copy of the other pointer is 0.
The read side leaves reset first; the write side leaves last, after the synchronized acknowledge is 0.
Words in the FIFO are discarded, and the storage is not cleared.

rules.condition: read accepted between i_rst_n_sw assertion and request arrival in read domain
rules.statement: Such a read returns a valid pre-reset word, which is discarded anyway.
A write is accepted only when i_wr_en is 1, wr_blk is 0 and the normal full condition is false.
A read is accepted only when i_rd_en is 1, rd_blk is 0 and the normal empty condition is false.
o_full is 1 while wr_blk; otherwise it is the normal full condition.

rules.condition: while wr_blk (write side) or rd_blk (read side)
rules.statement: o_full_thr and o_empty_thr take the values of an empty FIFO while blocked; otherwise normal.
No o_overflow or o_underflow pulse is generated for an access blocked by the software reset.
o_sw_rst_busy is set when the write FSM leaves RUN and cleared on return to RUN, equal to write FSM not in RUN at every clock edge.
The pointers are reset synchronously by the FSMs.
The FSM state registers are reset by the hardware resets i_rst_n_wr and i_rst_n_rd.

rules.condition: synchronized write pointer still old non-zero
rules.statement: The read side must not be released until the synchronized write pointer is 0, so no nonexistent word is read; likewise for the write side and full flag.
